text:
nora: Quick q: should rollout pins include an explicit hydration mode, or do we push rehydration to clients/probes? Trying to avoid surprise performance regressions during fast canaries.
alex: what's the exact desired outcome? full KV warm before routing, or just routing hints + lazy fill?
nora: Ideally we can opt into: 1) immediate KV warm (control-plane prefetch), 2) client probe (client hits a hydrate endpoint), or 3) off (lazy). Problem is cost + complexity if we prefetch.
ben: exposing a boolean is tempting (hydrate=true/false) but it's too simplistic. Enums give us more nuance. Also ops wants observability for when hydration runs.
tara: telemetry point: prefetches will create token spikes. We must tag traces with rollout_id and hydration mode so we can exclude them from normal latency/cost metrics.
javier: infra: prefetch means reading checkpoints and priming caches; synthetic requests emulate real patterns but may not distribute the same across model shards. Both have failure modes and quota impacts.
alex: proposal: add hydration enum: off | async_prefetch | client_probe. off=lazy; async_prefetch=control-plane fires background warm; client_probe=clients call /hydrate before routing.
nora: sounds reasonable. Can we keep the wire encoding compact (e.g. h=0/1/2) but surface names in UI/CLI?
ben: yes compact encoding is fine in metadata blobs, but APIs/console should be readable. Also define a failure contract: async_prefetch failure => fallback to lazy + alert. Don't make rollouts block on prefetch.
tara: add telemetry keys: rollout.hydration_mode (off/async/probe) and rollout.hydration_attempts (counter). Also annotate traces with rollout_id and hydration=true for prefetch runs.
javier: ops needs admin endpoints: /admin/hydration/status?rollout_id=... and /admin/hydration/abort?rollout_id=... Also enforce per-tenant throttles so a big rollout doesn't flood a GPU pool.
alex: example minimal pin shape (backwards compatible):
```
pin:
  model: gptx-3b
  variant: v2
  rollout_id: r-2026-03-23-42
  hydration: async_prefetch
```
nora: defaults idea: hosted free-tier = client_probe (cheap); enterprise Dedicated opt-in = async_prefetch. Document defaults and make override explicit.
ben: rollback UX: if we hydrated caches then rolled back, we need reclamation. But if hydration stamps each cached entry with release_id, clients/routers can ignore stale stamps so explicit dehydrate may not be required.
tara: agree — ensure hydrate attaches release_stamp; telemetry to show stale-hit rates.
javier: implementation checklist for infra: 1) bounded rate prefetchers, 2) fail-open policy (fallback to lazy), 3) admin status endpoints, 4) per-tenant budget checks.
nora: action items: 1) add hydration enum to pin schema (off/async_prefetch/client_probe), 2) add telemetry keys rollout.hydration_mode and rollout.hydration_attempts, 3) ops admin endpoints + throttles, 4) doc defaults per deployment. I'll draft a short RFC update + sample schema.

nora: thanks — I'll ping ops for quota numbers and then attach the diff. :thumbsup:
